Let me analyze this conflict.

Axis: applicant
- Register: "MinebeaMitsumi Inc."
- Document: "Minebea Co. Ltd."

Minebea Co. Ltd. and MinebeaMitsumi Inc. — historically, Minebea Co., Ltd. was renamed to MinebeaMitsumi Inc. in 2017. The certificate is from 2014, when the company was legally named "Minebea Co. Ltd." The register apparently has the current name "MinebeaMitsumi Inc."

Now, the rules given:
- spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity
- Extraction artifacts = document-noise
- Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since certificate is legal instrument)
- Number/year format differences = same-entity with register's canonical form

Is "MinebeaMitsumi Inc." vs "Minebea Co. Ltd." the same entity? Yes — it's the same corporate entity, just renamed. But the rule categories: "same-entity" applies to spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences. This is more than suffix drift — it's a name change (rebranding after merger with Mitsumi Electric). But fundamentally they ARE the same entity. The verdict options are: same-entity, different-entity, document-noise, unverifiable.

The entity is the same (Minebea Co. Ltd. renamed to MinebeaMitsumi Inc. after the 2017 merger with Mitsumi). So verdict = "same-entity".

Best value: For same-entity verdicts, the rules specify register canonical form for number/year differences. For name same-entity cases (spelling drift), presumably the register's canonical form is also preferred since the register is a database. The rules say for different-entity, best_value = document's value because certificate is legal instrument. For same-entity, it's implied best_value = register's canonical form (register is canonical).

Hmm, but wait — the certificate is the legal instrument, and at the time of issuance (2014), the legal name was "Minebea Co. Ltd." However, the rules define same-entity as best value from register (implied by "with the register's canonical form" for numbers). Actually the rules only explicitly give best_value guidance for document-noise (register), different-entity (document), and number/year same-entity (register). For name same-entity (spelling drift), the natural reading is register canonical form.

So: verdict "same-entity", best_value "MinebeaMitsumi Inc." (register's canonical form — the modern legal name of the same corporate entity), why: the 2014 certificate predates Minebea's 2017 merger/renaming to MinebeaMitsumi Inc., so both names denote the same corporate entity; the register carries the current canonical name.

One short sentence: "Minebea Co. Ltd. is the pre-2017 name of the same corporate entity later renamed MinebeaMitsumi Inc., so this is a name evolution, not a different company; keep the register's canonical form."
